activity.notes: Chisli is identified in scholarship on Mission San Diego as the Kwaaypaay, or leader, of Nipaguay and a key figure in the escalating conflict that culminated in the 1775 Kumeyaay revolt. ATLAS records the securely documented 1775 resistance context rather than inventing a longer chiefly reign.

sources.title: To Toil in That Vineyard of the Lord — Santa Clara University Faculty Book Gallery
sources.citation_text: The scholarly volume includes the chapter 'Chisli, Canuch, and Junípero Serra: Indian Responses to Mission San Diego, 1769–1788', establishing Chisli as a historical Kumeyaay figure in mission-era ethnohistory.

sources.title: Journal of San Diego History 68(2)
sources.citation_text: The journal cites the specialist scholarship on Chisli and the 1775 Mission San Diego revolt, including Sandos and Sandos and Richard Carrico's ethnohistorical study.
